newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM-Northwest deal paves way for higher profits.
newsitem.headline: KLM-Northwest deal paves way for higher profits.

text.p: Dutch airline KLM said on Wednesday the resolution of its long-running boardroom battle with U.S. partner Northwest paved the way for increased returns from their lucrative operational alliance.
KLM said earlier it would reduce its 18.8 percent voting stake in Northwest to zero by the year 2000 in a sell-back expected to raise between $1.07 billion to $1.17 billion.
"The alliance currently generates around $150 million dollars annually in terms of operating profits," KLM spokesman Hans Leijte said. "This can only increase."
Until now the partnership, under which the two airlines operate as one on transatlantic routes, has been based on a series of one-year contracts.

Longer term contracts enabling the two to take the necessary financial risks to extend the partnership have been held up by a protracted dispute over KLM's rights to a further five percent Northwest stake under an option exercisable in 1998.
KLM said on Wednesday it would drop its legal action to force Northwest to reverse a poison pill construction limiting its stake at current levels.
Leijte said there were as yet no firm plans for the proceeds of the Northwest stake sale.
"We have no special plans...it will of course bolster our liquidity position," he said.
Nor would the KLM spokesman give further details of plans to further intensify their cooperation in the air freight sector. "Details of the implementation will be released in due course," he said.
